open_questions: Why is the transit duration 1.676x the central duration for the 0.46 Rsun TIC star and fit_log_density_ratio -1.943 with star_density_penalty 206.8 - suggests high impact parameter or eccentricity versus stellar density error

Why is phase_curve amplitude 2344 ppm (1.097x depth) with chi2 159.4 for dof9 so large for a 2.34 Rearth planet - could be synchronous ellipsoidal/thermal effects vs unocculted spots on a variable M/K dwarf

Rotation period 1.322 d is essentially identical to orbital period 1.32 d (signal_over_rotation 1.000136) with stellar amplitude 11288 ppm in sector 22 - true tidally-synchronized hot planet vs phase-locked active star where transit period coincides with spot period by chance; needs RV/spot mapping to rule out spot modulation mimicking a 1.3 d transit
dossier.public_summary: TESS sees a small 2.3 Earth-radius dip repeating every 1.32 days on the M-dwarf target with a flat bottom and no secondary eclipse or off-target signal, which positively favours a planet. The transit is a bit too long for the star and the star varies strongly at the same period with a larger-than-expected out-of-transit swing, leaving the synchronization and stellar activity versus a planet as the remaining open question.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target; no star within 1 TESS pixel can produce the 2136 ppm dip with <25% eclipse, and all plausible Gaea neighbours are ruled out by >15 sigma, against a blended EB at a neighbour
